notes: Local income tax: Maryland county and Baltimore City income taxes (Form 502 lines 28-33; booklet PDF page 25, Instruction 19, 2025 Local Tax Rate Chart, .0225 to .0330 by county; Anne Arundel and Frederick counties use their own brackets, PDF pages 4-5) are local taxes, out of scope for now (tax-reference-data issue #1); not recorded as state brackets or surtaxes.

Brackets: Tax Rate Schedule I (single, married filing separately, dependent taxpayer, fiduciaries) is recorded under single and married_separate; Schedule II (joint, head of household, qualifying surviving spouse) under married_joint and head_of_household. The booklet says use the tax tables below 100,000 and the Worksheet Schedules (17A) at 100,000 or more, both based on these schedules. The schedule prints 'at least $1'; the first band is recorded from 0.

Brackets check: the schedules on PDF page 22 are printed again on PDF page 54 (estimated tax) with the same figures; the cumulative amounts (4,697.50; 5,947.50; 7,260.00; 12,760.00; 27,135.00; 58,385.00 and 7,072.50; 8,322.50; 10,947.50; 15,072.50; 32,322.50; 69,822.50) re-compute from the rates; tax table rows 20,000-20,050 = 899, 49,950-50,000 = 2,321 and 99,950-100,000 = 4,696 match the schedule at the row midpoint.

Printed typo: the Schedule I worksheet (17A) on PDF page 41 has a row 'At least $250,001 but not over $1,000,000' with subtraction amount 500,000.00, x .0625 and addition 27,135.00; the subtraction and addition amounts and Schedule I on PDF pages 22 and 54 show this is the 500,001 to 1,000,000 row. Recorded as 6.25% from 500,000.

Additional 2% tax on net capital gain income (new for 2025): federal AGI over 350,000 (one figure for every filing status) and capital gain income on Line 1c; 'certain' net capital gain income is taxed at .02 on Line 21b, on top of the rate schedule. Which gains are excluded ('net capital gain from the sale of certain assets is excluded', PDF page 53) is in Form 502CG and Technical Bulletin 58, not in these sources. Recorded under capital_gains, not surtaxes, because it applies to gains only.

Standard deduction: a flat amount by filing status (3,350 single, dependent and married filing separately; 6,700 joint, head of household, qualifying surviving spouse); the booklet prints no percentage, minimum or maximum. The dependent taxpayer status has no schema key; it shares the single amount.

Itemized deductions: allowed only if itemized on the federal return (FAQ 3, PDF page 7); state and local income taxes come out on Line 17b (that line is capped at 40,000, 20,000 married filing separately); itemized deductions are reduced by 7.5% of federal AGI over 200,000 (100,000 married filing separately), Instruction 14 and Worksheet 14A (PDF pages 20-21). The worksheet prints the two threshold blocks before their filing-status labels; the pairing follows the Instruction 14 sentence. No fixed amount, so recorded here only.

Exemptions: 3,200 per exemption for the filer and spouse and for each dependent, stepped down by federal AGI (Exemption Amount Chart 10A, recorded as a stepped phase_out); 1,000 each for the filer or spouse 65 or older or blind on the last day of the year, not reduced; a dependent taxpayer gets no personal exemption. Code hh (Worksheet 13C) lets filers with U.S. obligation interest recompute the exemption from federal AGI less that interest.

Dependent 65 or over: an additional exemption of 'up to $3,200' (Instruction 10); PDF page 53 says the dependent amount 'is doubled for allowable dependents age 65 or over'. The chart's reduction 'applies to the additional dependency exemptions as well', so the same stepped phase_out is recorded on both dependent entries.

Pension exclusion (Line 10a, Worksheet 13A): recorded as two entries, age 65 or older and totally disabled (self, or a spouse totally disabled), because the booklet's test is '65 or over or totally disabled, or your spouse was totally disabled'; one exclusion per individual (FAQ 1), so the two cannot combine. Whether 41,200 ('maximum allowable exclusion', on Worksheet 13E 'maximum Social Security benefit') is indexed is not stated.

Pension exclusion covers: qualified 401(a), 403 and 457(b) employee retirement systems; the booklet does not split public from private employers and does not limit public plans to Maryland, so public_pension, public_pension_other_state and private_pension are all listed (only the public safety subtraction, code v, excludes other states' personnel). Employer-plan distributions (401(k), 403(b), 457(b), Thrift Savings, SIMPLE 401(k)) qualify per the Form 502R chart. IRAs of every kind do not. Roth conversions are not addressed by name: covers_unclear. Whether military retirement above the code u amount can count is not stated; military_pension is not listed.

Retirement and age subtractions recorded: pension exclusion (Line 10a), retired forest/park/wildlife ranger exclusion (Line 10b), military retirement (code u), public safety retirement (code v), state pension pickup (code r), fire/police job-injury pension payments (code a), fire/police survivor payments (code aa), centenarian income (code ya), U.S. obligation income (code ab), two-income married couple subtraction (Line 14), Social Security and railroad retirement (Line 11). Not recorded: the other Form 502SU codes, none of which is a retirement or age rule (child care Line 9, military overseas pay code p, volunteer police/fire code va, length-of-service awards code n, education, ABLE, adoption, foster care, teacher supplies, union dues, Build America Bond interest code ii, Maryland bond sale profit code e, and others).

Military retirement (code u): 20,000 at 55 or older, 12,500 under 55, each on the last day of the taxable year; 'under the age of 55' is recorded as max_age 54 (age reached). The booklet prints 'at lest 55 years of age' (typo for 'least'). The booklet does not say whether these caps interact with the Line 10a exclusion beyond keeping code u amounts off Worksheet 13A line 1.

Public safety retirement (code v): up to 15,000, 55 or older; retired correctional, law enforcement, fire, rescue or emergency services personnel of the United States, Maryland or a Maryland subdivision; the booklet does not say 'contributory'.

Retired ranger exclusion (Line 10b): 55 or over and not 65 or older (recorded as max_age 64), not totally disabled and no totally disabled spouse; one spouse may take Line 10a and the other Line 10b, but one individual may not take both.

Social Security: 'Social Security and railroad retirement benefits are exempt from state tax' (Instruction 13 Line 11, PDF page 16); Form 502 Line 11 subtracts the taxable Social Security and RR benefits included in Line 1. Recorded as exempt, and as an exempt_in_full relief.

Municipal interest: Line 2 adds interest on non-Maryland state and local obligations (including through mutual funds); interest on Maryland and Maryland subdivision obligations is exempt (PDF page 13). Interest on U.S. obligations is subtracted (code ab; not GNMA).
Indexing: the booklet text has no statement on inflation adjustment of any figure (searched for inflation, indexed, adjusted annually, cost of living); not_stated.
Recapture: none printed; the schedules are marginal. The exemption step-down is held in the exemption phase_out.

Two-income married couple subtraction (Line 14, Worksheet 13D): joint return, both spouses with income subject to Maryland tax; the smaller of 1,200 and the lower spouse's federal AGI plus additions less subtractions. covers all_income as the nearest kind.
